# Fresh physics/operator/probability consequences — 7 October 2026

## Outcome and status

The most useful positive mechanism is an exact reconstruction of Gaussian cycle phases from **charge weighted modular commutators**. On a rectangular square grid it uses pair spectra and one four-site probe per face, instead of requiring a nonzero covariance link from one root to every site. It has a complete elementary derivation below. These are additional observables: they are not obtainable automatically from the spectra and ordinary modular commutators in the attached A–F interface. Historical novelty and an economical physical acquisition protocol remain UNKNOWN.

Two negative results materially delimit this opportunity.

* For half-filled Gaussian covariances supported on any bipartite graph, every ordinary modular commutator vanishes. Opposite nonreal loop phases are indistinguishable even by every ordered many-body word made only from the state's modular Hamiltonians. A one-particle Jordan–Lie expression detects the phase, but its genuine many-body analogue cancels exactly.
* The naive photon-number entropy inequality conditioned on arbitrary quantum memory is false even for a fixed independent thermal bath, positive conditional input entropy, and three finite-energy Gaussian modes. The explicit example below has a certified violation greater than 0.0269 nats. It does not contradict release family 273, whose interface is independent input ports without conditioning on the memory.

Exact local cycle recovery also fails to furnish a size-independent Lipschitz inverse: a constant edge floor and a fixed covariance spectral margin do not prevent weak face errors from accumulating around a large grid boundary.

These are complementary to the root's repetition and spectral-collision teams. They do not resolve the imported collision theorem, yield quantum PCP, or establish a new post-release computational capability. The cycle mechanism uses standard Gaussian calculus and cycle invariants rather than a load-bearing theorem unique to the new release.
